No fee is expected. Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26), effective 9 March 2026, lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion and provides 'Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee' in both Superior and District Court. The $60 post-judgment motion fee on that schedule is tied by its own terms to M.R. Civ. P. 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66, which are civil rules, and does not reach a criminal post-judgment motion. Confirm with the clerk and do not promise a refund.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Maine criminal history record from the State Bureau of Identification. requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

Check your answer to "Have you arranged to get three standard fingerprint cards from a local law enforcement agency? You need them before you file." against Three standard fingerprint cards, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Arrest report or booking record. Make an open-records request to the arresting agency for the arrest or booking record. It supplies the date of arrest, the citation number, the offense charged and the agency name, all of which § 610.123 makes mandatory contents of the petition.
Check your answer to "On what date were you arrested?" against Arrest report or booking record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the entry disposing of each offense related to the arrest. The ground requires that every related offense or violation was nolle prossed, dismissed or acquitted, so the participant needs the disposition for each one, not just the lead charge.

Check your answer to "If you are relying on the moving-violation ground: was every offense or violation connected to that arrest nolle prossed, dismissed, or did you get a not-guilty finding on each? If even one is outstanding or resulted in a conviction, this ground does not apply." against Certified record of the dismissal, nolle prosequi or not-guilty finding, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based. Order a fingerprint-based search of your own record. It is how the participant builds the agency list and confirms the prior-and-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol before ordering.

Check your answer to "Have you been convicted of any misdemeanor or felony, before or after this arrest?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record. It shows the offense classification and whether a commercial driver licence was ever issued, and commercial licence status at the time of arrest is an outright bar on the moving-violation ground.

Check your answer to "At the time of the arrest, did you hold a commercial driver licence, or were you driving a commercial motor vehicle? Answer for the time of the arrest, not for now." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

The petitioner signs the sworn statement on CR145 page 2 — I swear the facts stated in the above petition are true according to my best knowledge and belief — in the presence of the officer administering the oath. requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Missouri Department of Revenue driver record. Order your Missouri driver record from the Department of Revenue. It is the document that shows administrative suspensions and revocations under §§ 302.500 to 302.540 and chemical-test refusals, which are alcohol-related enforcement contacts under § 302.525.3 even where no conviction followed. A participant who answers the enforcement-contact question from memory will very often be wrong.

Check your answer to "Since then, has your driving licence been suspended or revoked for anything alcohol-related, in Missouri or any other state — including for refusing a breath, blood or urine test? This counts even if you were never convicted of anything, and it is the question people most often answer wrongly." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Out-of-state driver records. Request your driver record from each state where you have been licensed. § 302.525.3 counts a suspension, revocation or conviction in any other state, and § 610.130.4 bars anyone issued or required to hold a commercial driver's licence in any state.

Check your answer to "Have you ever been issued a commercial driver's licence, in Missouri or in any other state, or are you required to hold one for your work? This bars the whole section, whether or not it had anything to do with the offense." against Out-of-state driver records, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified docket sheet and judgment from the court of plea or sentence. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and the judgment. It establishes the plea or sentencing date the ten-year period runs from, the offense level, and the case number.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record. Order your own criminal record. It supports the agency list and the no-subsequent-conviction condition. Confirm current fees with the Patrol.

Check your answer to "Since that plea or conviction, have you been convicted of any other drink- or drug-driving offense or intoxication-related boating offense, in Missouri or any other state?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Case.net printout for each case. Search Case.net by your name, and by every name variant and spelling you have used, for every county you have lived in or been charged in. Print the case summary and the docket for each matter. Case.net does not show every municipal division, so it is a starting point rather than a complete record.

Check your answer to "List every Missouri case you want expunged: the case number, the court name, the approximate date of the charge, the county or municipality where it was charged, and a description of the charge. Every crime you want expunged has to be in this one petition." against Case.net printout for each case, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case. Ask the clerk of each court for a certified copy of the docket sheet and the judgment or final disposition. A per-page or per-document fee usually applies. This is the document that proves the case number, the court, the offense description and the disposition date.

Check your answer to "For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date." against Certified docket sheet and judgment for each case, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Probation or parole discharge document. Ask your former probation or parole officer, or the Division of Probation and Parole, for the discharge document showing the date supervision ended. The waiting period runs from the day you completed the authorized disposition, and for a supervised case that is usually this date.

Check your answer to "For each case, on what date did you finish everything the court ordered — the end of any jail or prison term, the end of probation or parole, and the last payment of any fine, cost or restitution? This is the date the waiting period runs from, not the arrest date and not the conviction date." against Probation or parole discharge document, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution. Ask the clerk for the payment history on each case, showing a zero balance. Paragraph 3 of CR360 has you swear that all obligations relating to the disposition are satisfied, including fines and restitution, and an unpaid balance is a common and avoidable reason a petition is dismissed.

Check your answer to "Have you paid every fine, court cost and restitution order in full on each of those cases?" against Receipts or a clerk's payment history for fines, costs and restitution, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record. Request your own criminal record through MACHS. A name-based search shows open records; a fingerprint-based search is the only way to see records that are already closed, including anything already closed by law under § 610.105. Confirm the current fees with the Patrol before ordering, and note that fingerprint capture carries a separate vendor service fee.

Check your answer to "Have you ever been granted a Missouri expungement before? If so, list the court and case number, and say whether each was a felony, a misdemeanor or an ordinance violation with a possible jail term, or an infraction." against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "Is any case on your list a class A felony, a dangerous felony, an offense that required sex-offender registration, a felony where death was an element, a felony assault, any domestic assault, a felony kidnapping, a chapter 566 sex offense, a drink- or drug-driving or boating offense, an aircraft intoxication offense, an ordinance violation equivalent to any of those, a motor-vehicle offense while you held or were required to hold a commercial driver licence, or an unlawful use of weapons offense under § 571.030?" against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Any statement that a particular offense is or is not on the § 610.140.3 exclusion list — Not present in the packet at all.

none. CR360 uses a declaration under penalty of perjury rather than a notarial acknowledgment. This is the opposite of CR145 on the § 610.122 track, which must be subscribed and sworn before a notary, judge or clerk, and the two must not be conflated in participant copy.

Standard circuit court filing fees and costs apply, and they vary by county. Rule 155.02 governs filing fees and costs for an expungement action. The exact current amount is county-variable and is confirmed with the clerk; costs may also include service, copying, certification and record-retrieval charges. The participant separately pays for the Highway Patrol record and for certified copies.

A petition filed with the clerk of the Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.2(1)). Rule 155.01 commences the action by filing a petition in the circuit court of the county in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty. Every crime sought to be expunged must be in the one petition (§ 610.140.2(2)). FI-05 is filed with it. Whether any circuit rejects the statewide CR360 in favour of a local form is unresolved, which is why the track carries a local-form override and a clerk-contact step.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Certified docket sheet and the entry dismissing the charge or the not-guilty judgment. Ask the clerk for a certified copy of the docket and of the entry disposing of the charge. It establishes which of the two routes applies, and if an expungement order was already entered under § 610.145.1(2) the docket is where you will see it.

Check your answer to "How did the charge against you end — was it dismissed, or were you found not guilty at trial? If it was dismissed because of the identity problem, Missouri law says the prosecutor or judge should have told the court and the court should have expunged it without you filing anything." against Certified docket sheet and the entry dismissing the charge or the not-guilty judgment, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that the identity was used without permission, or that a misidentification occurred. Gather whatever shows the case was not yours: a police report naming another person, an identity-theft report you filed, correspondence from the prosecutor, a court entry recording the mistake, employment or travel records placing you elsewhere. LegalEase never sees, holds or assesses this; the court decides whether it is enough.

Check your answer to "What proof do you have that this was not you — a police report naming someone else, an identity-theft report, a letter from the prosecutor, a court entry, an alibi record? You do not need it to prepare the petition, but the court will want to see it." against Proof that the identity was used without permission, or that a misidentification occurred, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "Did this matter affect your driving licence — points, a suspension or a revocation? If so the order requires the Department of Revenue to reverse it and to give you a corrected driving history and a reinstatement at no cost." against Missouri Department of Revenue driver record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "Have you asked the clerk of that court whether an expungement order was already entered when the charge was dismissed?" against Missouri State Highway Patrol criminal record, fingerprint-based, and correct the packet if they disagree.
Any assertion that the participant's identity was used without permission — CR301, recited only from the participant's own account.

Any assertion that a witness or law-enforcement officer misidentified the participant, was confused, was misinformed or made some other mistake — CR301, recited only from the participant's own account.

The petitioner swears or affirms under penalty of perjury that the facts are true according to their best knowledge and belief, and signs. LegalEase leaves the signature and date blank.
none prescribed by § 610.145 or by CR301, which uses a sworn or affirmed statement rather than a notarial acknowledgment.

The costs of expunging the records, as provided in chapter 610, shall not be taxed against the person eligible for expungement under this section (§ 610.145.3). Any reinstatement fee for a licence or privilege is waived (§ 610.145.5). Whether a court nonetheless collects an opening filing fee where the petition commences a new case is not addressed by the section and is confirmed with the clerk. No fee figure is published on this track.

Ordinarily unnecessary, because § 610.145.3 provides that costs are not taxed against the eligible person. GN10 under Rule 77.03 and § 514.040 is available where a court nevertheless requires an opening fee the participant cannot pay.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain FBI Identity History Summary. Request an Identity History Summary from the FBI and pay the FBI's fee. Check your answer to "For each conviction, what are the case number, the court, the arresting agency, the charge and the date?" against FBI Identity History Summary, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain New Mexico Department of Public Safety Record of Arrest and Prosecution (RAP) sheet. Complete the DPS Authorization for Release of Information, have it notarized with an original signature, and send it to DPS with a $15.00 money order or cashier's check per record check. It must be dated no later than ninety days before filing.

Check your answer to "For each conviction, what are the case number, the court, the arresting agency, the charge and the date?" against New Mexico Department of Public Safety Record of Arrest and Prosecution (RAP) sheet, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Judgment and sentence, and proof that the sentence was completed. Ask the clerk of the court that entered the conviction for the judgment and sentence, and ask probation or parole for a discharge document. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(a) asks for documentation showing completion of the sentences for the convictions you are seeking to expunge.

Check your answer to "On what date did you finish the sentence for each conviction, including any probation or parole?" against Judgment and sentence, and proof that the sentence was completed, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that sentences for any other convictions were completed. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(b) asks for documentation showing completion of sentences for any other convictions served. Because the waiting period runs from the most recent sentence completed in any jurisdiction, gather this for out-of-state convictions too.

Check your answer to "Have you completed a sentence for any conviction in any other state, or in a federal, tribal or military court — and if so, when did the most recent one end?" against Proof that sentences for any other convictions were completed, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof of final payment of fines and fees. Ask the clerk or the collections office for a receipt or a zero-balance statement for the conviction you want cleared. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(c) asks for it.

Check your answer to "Have you paid all fines and fees owed for the conviction you want cleared, and on what date was the final payment made?" against Proof of final payment of fines and fees, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that victim restitution was completed. Ask the court or the restitution administrator for a document showing restitution was paid in full. Form 4-953 paragraph 17(d) asks for it and Section 29-3A-5(C)(3) makes it a finding the court must make.

Check your answer to "Was victim restitution ordered in connection with the conviction, and have you finished paying it?" against Proof that victim restitution was completed, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Docket sheet or other record detailing the offenses. Use the New Mexico Courts "Find a Case" search to locate the case, then ask the clerk for the docket sheet. Court copies run about $0.35 per page.

participantActionRequired.description: The sections prescribe none. On the subsection 1 branch there is nothing to serve. On the subsection 2 branch the sections require only "the filing of a petition by the defendant" and name no person to be served; the Division is the body given the right to object, and whether the petition must be served on it or on the prosecutor is not established by the text and is recorded as an open question.

Two mechanisms in one track. On the subsection 1 branch nothing is filed by the participant: the justice court, municipal court or district court orders the sealing itself after the discharge or dismissal, without a hearing, unless the Division petitions for good cause not to seal. On the subsection 2 branch the defendant files a petition in the court that handled the case, and not sooner than seven years after the conditional dismissal or the setting aside of the judgment.

$250 solicitor administrative fee per individual order under § 17-22-940(A), nonrefundable even if the charge is later found ineligible; $25 SLED verification fee under § 17-22-940(E)(1); and the $35 clerk of court filing fee under § 17-22-940(F) and § 8-21-310(C)(4), which the solicitor forwards and which is refunded if the charge is found statutorily ineligible.

$250 solicitor administrative fee per individual order under § 17-22-940(A), nonrefundable even if the charge is later found ineligible; $25 SLED verification fee under § 17-22-940(E)(1); and the $35 clerk of court filing fee under § 17-22-940(F) and § 8-21-310(C)(4), which the solicitor forwards and which is refunded if the charge is found statutorily ineligible. No $250 solicitor administrative fee, unless the charge was dismissed, discharged or nolle prossed as part of the plea arrangement under which the defendant pled guilty and was sentenced to other charges, in which case the $250 applies. A clerk's fee applies. Section 40-32-106(d)(3) requires the appropriate clerk's fee pursuant to T.C.A. § 8-21-401 for destroying the records, which is the asymmetry a participant should be warned about: diversion is a non-conviction outcome but it is not free, whereas a straight dismissal is. The amount is set by § 8-21-401 and no figure is quoted here.

No indigency or fee-waiver provision appears in the reorganized §§ 40-32-106 to 40-32-110. The TBI operates an unpublished indigency procedure for its separate diversion certificate fee, requiring a form signed by the judge that it supplies on request and does not publish. No waiver mechanism for the clerk's expunction fee was identified.

The petitioner signs and the petition must be verified under art. 55A.253. Both a notarial verification block and an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury are provided, and county practice chooses between them.
Verification is required by statute. Whether an unsworn declaration satisfies it is accepted in practice by some clerks and not others, which is why both blocks ship.

Read at source on 2026-08-06. Article 102.006, the old expunction fee statute, was repealed by S.B. 1667 effective 2025-09-01, temporarily re-added by H.B. 16 of the 89th Legislature 2nd Called Session with a built-in expiry, and permanently replaced by art. 102.0061 effective 2026-01-01. Under art. 102.0061(a) a district court charges the fee that applies to filing an ex parte petition in a civil action in district court, which is the ordinary county civil filing fee and is not a flat statutory amount; under (b) a justice court or municipal court of record charges a flat $100. Separately, art. 55A.254(e) forbids the clerk charging anything to transmit the petition or notice of hearing electronically, and art. 55A.254(f) requires the clerk to charge $25 for each listed entity unable to receive an electronic transmission, with the same structure repeated at the order stage under art. 55A.351(b-2) and (b-3). The number of paper-only agencies a packet names is therefore a direct dollar cost to the participant. The packet does not quote the old $250 to $500 range, which is no longer reliable. On this track specifically, art. 102.0061(c) requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal.

A Statement of Inability to Afford Payment of Court Costs under Tex. R. Civ. P. 145, filed with the petition. The Supreme Court of Texas has approved a bilingual statewide form in Misc. Docket No. 22-9090, and Rule 145 requires the clerk to make it available without charge or request. This is the only genuinely statewide promulgated form in the entire Texas record-clearing workflow. Article 102.0061(c) separately requires the fee to be waived where the expunction relates to an acquittal other than one described by art. 55A.151 and the petition is filed not later than the 30th day after the acquittal, and (d) requires waiver of the district-court fee where entitlement arises under art. 55A.053(a)(2)(A) or (B).

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Texas DPS criminal history record. Follow DPS form CR-63, the Procedure for Review of Personal Criminal History Record Information. It is an instruction sheet rather than a form to complete: it sets out fingerprinting through the DPS FAST vendor at a $10 fingerprinting fee plus a $15 record fee, or a hard-card mail route. The DPS history supplies the TRN the order must carry under art. 55A.301, the arrest date, the arresting agency and the agency list, and it is also how the participant sees whether relief already happened. DPS states it may oppose an expunction petition and that its legal staff cannot assist with one.
participantActionRequired.obtainedFrom: Texas Department of Public Safety Crime Records Service

participantActionRequired.description: Check your answer to "Do you have your DPS criminal history? The incident number it carries, the TRN, has to go on the order." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain The district clerk's published list of agencies and e-mail addresses. Article 55A.253(c) requires each district clerk to compile and maintain this list on the clerk's website. Ask for it by name. The clerk is not responsible for the list being complete, so it is a starting point rather than an answer, and every e-mail address on it saves the participant $25 per stage.

participantActionRequired.description: The clerk sends the petition and notice of hearing by certified mail return receipt requested, or by secure e-mail, electronic transmission or fax. requiredBeforeFiling: Check your answer to "List every other conviction and every other deferred adjudication you have ever had, with dates, other than fine-only traffic offences." against Texas DPS criminal history record, and correct the packet if they disagree.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI. Submit the BCI Application for Expungement of Adult Criminal History with the application fee, or with a fee waiver request. BCI checks governmental records including national criminal databases and may review previously expunged records from any jurisdiction. If eligible, BCI issues the certificate on payment of the issuance fee. File the court packet within 180 days of issuance.

Check your answer to "If BCI has already issued your certificate of eligibility, what date did it issue? It is valid for 180 days and must still be valid on the day you file." against Certificate of eligibility issued by BCI, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full. Ask the clerk of the sentencing court for a current balance on the case, and check with the Office of State Debt Collection if any balance was entered as a civil judgment and transferred. An unpaid balance defeats the petition and will also defeat the BCI certificate.

Check your answer to "Have all fines, fees, interest and restitution on this case been paid in full?" against Proof that fines, fees, interest and restitution are paid in full, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "List every criminal case you have ever had, in any state, including cases that were already expunged. BCI reviews all of them when it decides your certificate." against The participant's own case history for every case in every state, including previously expunged cases, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Certified copy of the judgment of acquittal. Ask the clerk of the trial court for a certified copy of the judgment of acquittal. It carries the acquittal date and shows which charges it covered.
Check your answer to "What is the date of the acquittal?" against Certified copy of the judgment of acquittal, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Check your answer to "When you look the case up on My Court Case, does it still show, or does it show as expunged?" against My Court Case record showing whether the case has already been expunged, and correct the packet if they disagree.

The petitioner's signature and date on the petition — Petition, signature block.

The petitioner signs the petition. The proposed order is completed by the petitioner except for the judge's signature line, which is left blank. This is the one Vermont track with a filing fee. Under 32 V.S.A. § 1431(e), read at source on 2026-08-06, the $90 filing fee applies only to a motion to seal a criminal history record of a violation of 23 V.S.A. § 1201(a) and does not apply to any other motion to seal or expunge under 13 V.S.A. § 7602, 33 V.S.A. § 5119(g) or other records-clearance provisions. Two currency problems attach and are carried as a release blocker rather than resolved: § 1431(e) still cross-references 13 V.S.A. § 7602(a)(1)(C), a subdivision Act 60 eliminated, and the Judiciary's own gloss that the fee applies where the offence was committed at 25 or older has no anchor in the current § 7602 text. The packet therefore states that a fee applies on this track and directs the participant to the Judiciary fee page rather than asserting an amount or an age condition.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory. Ask the clerk of the county of disposition for a certified copy of the disposition, the judgment order and the sentencing order for each case. Most counties charge a per-copy fee. Ask for every case, not only the one you came in for, because the petition is once per lifetime.

Check your answer to "List every West Virginia conviction on your record, however old, including traffic citations — not just the one you came here about. What was each offence, in which county, and on what date were you convicted?" against Certified disposition, judgment order and sentencing order for every conviction on the inventory, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Proof of supervision completion. Ask the probation office that supervised you for written confirmation of the date supervision ended, and the institution of confinement for the date of release. The waiting period runs from the later of conviction, release and end of supervision, so this date is usually the one that decides eligibility.

Check your answer to "For each conviction, on what date did you finish any jail or prison term and any probation, parole or other supervision?" against Proof of supervision completion, and correct the packet if they disagree.

Obtain Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order. Ask the clerk of the court that entered the order for a copy. The statute requires a current order to be attached to the petition; a past order is disclosed but not attached.

Check your answer to "Is there now, or has there ever been, an order for restitution, protection, a restraining order or another no-contact order stopping you contacting a victim in any of these cases?" against Copy of any current restitution, protection, restraining or no-contact order, and correct the packet if they disagree.
